title: Female Workforce Participation in Emerging Industries and Sectors with Dearth of Women Talents
what_it_is: Female Workforce Participation in Emerging Industries and Sectors with Dearth of Women Talents

sections.label: Women's employment and pay gap
sections.summary: Female employment, PMET share and STEM share rose over the decade, and a 2019 MOM-NUS study linked occupational gender ratios to traits, skills, flexibility values and social norms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Singapore's female employment rate has increased over the past decade from 54% in 2010 to 57.7% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Women's share amongst Professional Managers, Executives and Technicians (PMETs) has also increased over the decade, from 41.1% to 45.6%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We are observing more women joining growth sectors such as in information and communication, financial services and health and social services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Altogether, women make up 52.8% in these three sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The share of women in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) jobs, while lower, has also increased from 29.9% in 2015, to 32.4% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: In 2019, MOM conducted a joint study on Singapore's suggested gender pay gap with Assoc Prof Jessica Pan from NUS and the study found that the differences in gender ratios across occupations could be due to gender differences in terms of personality and psychological traits, skills, different values placed on workplace flexibility, as well as social norms.
